trigger_condition: The single crash-recovery retry returns 429 (a PodDisruptionBudget blocks it) or the pod still runs afterwards
guard_snippet: else retry_result in (429, still_running) -> status=Failed or ambiguous; escalate(FR-31); no further retry
potential_consequence: Recovery after the one allowed retry is undefined, so a loop or silent stall is possible

trigger_condition: The executor crashes again during the recovery retry, with no new intent recorded
guard_snippet: write status attempt=2 intent before retry; on restart if attempt>=2 and no result -> ambiguous
potential_consequence: After a second restart, attempt 1 and the retry can't be told apart, so retries could repeat without limit

trigger_condition: Eviction returns 429 because a PodDisruptionBudget blocks it, during normal (non-crash) execution
guard_snippet: on 429: record blocked; bounded backoff within approval validity; then Failed -> person
potential_consequence: The run stalls or retries without limit, holding claims and approval validity

trigger_condition: A 409 precondition failure, then a re-read shows a different UID or resourceVersion
guard_snippet: if reread.uid != D.target_uid -> void run, require new request version; if only resourceVersion changed -> revalidate preconditions
potential_consequence: What happens after the re-read is unstated, so the executor might act on a changed or replacement target

trigger_condition: An expired claim's work can never be confirmed (target node lost, API down, ambiguous run)
guard_snippet: if claim expired and confirmation impossible for > T -> escalate to person; person may release claim (audited)
potential_consequence: The claim is held forever, blocking every repair in that scope with no escalation

trigger_condition: The audit service is unreachable or rejects the intent append before the action
guard_snippet: if audit.append(intent) fails -> do not act; status=blocked(audit); escalate
potential_consequence: The action runs unrecorded, contradicting 'no repair runs unrecorded'

trigger_condition: Verification after an action is inconclusive because Prometheus or the logs are stale or down
guard_snippet: if verification signals stale/missing -> status=unverified; treat as ambiguous -> person
potential_consequence: An unverifiable result could be recorded as Succeeded, or left pending with no handling

trigger_condition: The workload restarts the target, so each new pod has a new UID
guard_snippet: count repeats per entry and owning workload (controller UID), not per pod UID
potential_consequence: The repeat cap is never reached, so the same repair repeats on every replacement pod

trigger_condition: A valid stop arrives while the approved action is already executing
guard_snippet: define: stop received mid-run -> abort before next step; completed step verified and recorded; no further steps
potential_consequence: It's unclear whether 'stop beats go' interrupts a multi-step repair already in progress

trigger_condition: The first approval's validity lapses while the second approver is being re-asked
guard_snippet: start = min(valid_until of all approvals); if any lapsed -> re-ask each lapsed approver
potential_consequence: A repair could start on an approval that has already expired

trigger_condition: Unanswered requests never expire, while the quota caps open runs (AD-2)
guard_snippet: exclude awaiting-approval requests from the run quota, or escalate and close stale requests at quota
potential_consequence: Unanswered requests use up the quota and block new automatic repairs

trigger_condition: The status-statement age is exactly 1 h or exactly 24 h
guard_snippet: Fresh: age < 1h; Stale: 1h <= age < 24h; Expired: age >= 24h
potential_consequence: The tier boundaries overlap, so which tier applies (and what may run) is ambiguous at the boundary

trigger_condition: The cluster clock jumps backward or drifts while offline, and the statement age is computed from that clock
guard_snippet: measure statement age with monotonic clock since receipt; if clock unsynchronised -> treat tier as Expired
potential_consequence: An old status statement still looks fresh, bypassing the offline limits

trigger_condition: The clock is unsynchronised and Fleet and NTP are unreachable, so skew can't be measured
guard_snippet: if last successful sync age > max or skew unknown -> unsynchronised=true
potential_consequence: There's no default for unknown skew, so time-limited approvals could be accepted wrongly

trigger_condition: The SMS attempt or resend limits run out, or the roster person has no phone number
guard_snippet: on limit exhausted or no roster phone -> request stays open, status 'confirmation blocked', notify admins
potential_consequence: No state is defined after the limits run out, so the request could hang or be silently downgraded

trigger_condition: Protected storage is full, audit space is also exhausted, then a stop arrives
guard_snippet: reserve audit space for stops; if exhausted, apply stop anyway and record loss in heartbeat
potential_consequence: The stop is refused, contradicting 'stop beats go'

trigger_condition: The outbox reaches its size limit for non-reserved traffic, or the reserved capacity for stops and receipts fills
guard_snippet: on full: drop oldest reports (count into coverage); reserved full -> block new requests, escalate
potential_consequence: No drop or overflow policy is defined, so messages may be lost silently or stops blocked

trigger_condition: etcd is restored from a backup or the cluster is reinstalled, rolling back the ledger
guard_snippet: on ledger epoch regression -> refuse all signed objects until fresh relay status and key list fetched
potential_consequence: Used decision_ids and highest versions roll back, so old decisions could be replayed

trigger_condition: The node's management mode or repair configuration can't be determined (API error, unknown setup)
guard_snippet: default row: mode unknown -> no node actions; detect, evidence, escalate
potential_consequence: The mode table has no default, so the executor might act on a node AWS is repairing

trigger_condition: First install, or no rollback-safe previous release exists, so there is no recovery version
guard_snippet: if no pre-authorised recovery version -> guard inert; probation failure -> person
potential_consequence: What the guard does with no recovery target is undefined

trigger_condition: The final wave has no not-yet-updated clusters to compare against, or a platform has none left
guard_snippet: if comparison cohort empty -> compare to pre-update baseline of same clusters
potential_consequence: The health comparison has no baseline, so the last wave goes unchecked or stalls

trigger_condition: Rollout data stays missing or stale indefinitely
guard_snippet: if paused > T -> alert Orvex release owner; require explicit resume or stop
potential_consequence: A rollout can stay paused indefinitely with nobody notified

trigger_condition: A new problem group has no history, so its 'normal rate' is undefined
guard_snippet: if no baseline -> use fixed minimum threshold for urgent alert
potential_consequence: A new fleet-wide failure may never cross the threshold, so no alert fires

trigger_condition: A customer admin changes settings (ticks, modes) on the local dashboard while the cluster is offline or Expired
guard_snippet: local dashboard: narrowing-only changes (untick, alert-only, withdraw); widening needs portal plus option B
potential_consequence: Local settings changes could widen automatic repair authority without SMS confirmation

trigger_condition: A target cluster's request version or nonce changes between submitting its leaf and the group approval
guard_snippet: leaf mismatch -> cluster refuses, reports 'needs re-approval'; console shows per-cluster refusal
potential_consequence: The cluster silently drops out of the group while the console still shows it covered
